$comment: Scenario backlog: agreed question seeds that are not yet written. This is authoring input, not app content — the runner never loads this file. A seed graduates when the questions exist in a quiz-data question file, at which point set status to "written" and list the ids. Seeds came from the second- and third-wave source reviews; see data-sources/SOURCES.md for the sources themselves. competencies are taxonomy ids and are validated against taxonomy/competencies.json; types and difficulty are intentions, not commitments. Naming: composites use fictional cities — Cedar Landing (~5,100, downtown redevelopment) and Riverbend (~38,000, fiscal cliff) exist in case-studies/; Rowan Falls (~9,000, state-route main street) is referenced by four questions whose case study has not landed yet. Third-wave composites add Ashgrove, Little Vernon, Fairhaven, Millbrook, Wexford, Copper Mesa, Bay Point and Tallow County, each tied to a community_type from taxonomy/community-types.json.

seeds.title: The reserve floor
seeds.summary: Council wants to fund a popular recurring program by drawing the general fund balance below the adopted reserve policy floor for three consecutive years, arguing the policy is a guideline rather than a limit. Manager must sequence a response.

seeds.title: Fines and fees drift
seeds.summary: Over eight years a city's citation revenue has grown from 2% to 11% of general fund revenue while the code enforcement division's stated mission remained compliance, not revenue. The finance director's forecast now assumes that revenue continues.
grounding: GFOA Rethinking Revenue — fines and fees
seeds.note: Pairs with the Cedar Landing enforcement case, case-studies/downtown-vacancy-carrots-and-sticks.md.

seeds.title: The decision architect
seeds.summary: Mid-sized city moves off line-item budgeting. Five departments, one budget officer, competing definitions of what “priority” means.

seeds.title: Structural, not one-time
seeds.summary: Given a revenue and expenditure table, separate structural from one-time gap components and size the recurring correction.
grounding: EMMA official statements, for realistic magnitudes
seeds.note: A driver for the numeric-multi type: the teaching point is the decomposition, not one figure.

seeds.title: The commercial TIF offset
seeds.summary: A council majority wants a commercial TIF district on the strength of assessed value growth inside comparable districts. Manager knows the growth may be displaced rather than created, and that the answer differs for industrial use.
grounding: Merriman, Lincoln Institute of Land Policy — Improving Tax Increment Financing

seeds.title: Four strategies, one staff
seeds.summary: A 4,500-person town is simultaneously pursuing industrial recruitment, business retention, residential development, and partnership-building with two nonprofits, on 1.5 FTE of economic development capacity.
grounding: UNC School of Government — Farmville NC profile

seeds.title: Shrinking, not growing
seeds.summary: Vacant and abandoned properties in a declining neighborhood. Options include demolition, land banking, green infrastructure conversion, and hold-for-market. Infrastructure is sized for a population that left.
grounding: EPA Saginaw MI land use and infrastructure strategy (2014)
seeds.note: Fills a real gap: every current case assumes a growth or recovery frame.

seeds.title: Broadband as economic development
seeds.summary: Small town weighing municipal broadband against an incumbent-partnership model, with a state preemption question hanging over it.
grounding: UNC School of Government — Houston MN and Tryon NC profiles

seeds.title: Who pays for hydrants
seeds.summary: A court holds that fire hydrant costs are a general government responsibility, not a water utility one. The utility has been carrying them for years; the general fund has no room. A rate study is already underway.

seeds.title: Indirect cost allocation
seeds.summary: General fund charges the enterprise fund for central services; the methodology has not been revisited in nine years and appears to over-allocate. Fixing it opens a hole in the general fund.
grounding: Seattle Public Utilities performance audit findings
seeds.note: A driver for the numeric-multi type: allocation split plus the resulting general fund gap.

seeds.title: Keep the asphalt plant?
seeds.summary: Make-versus-buy on a municipal asphalt operation. Aging equipment, a specialized crew, and a bid market with two regional suppliers.
grounding: San Francisco Public Works municipal asphalt plant study

seeds.title: Minimum staffing versus outcomes
seeds.summary: Fire minimum staffing is contractually fixed; response-time outcomes have not moved in five years; a station relocation would help more than added staff.
grounding: ICMA Center for Performance Measurement case study reports

seeds.title: Deferred maintenance backlog
seeds.summary: Pavement condition index has fallen for six years. Council will fund one of: full-depth reconstruction of the worst arterial, preventive sealing across the network, or a fleet replacement cycle that keeps crews operational.
grounding: Oakland Public Works Agency performance audit

seeds.title: The data culture problem
seeds.summary: A dashboard exists, nobody uses it, and a department head disputes the numbers in a public meeting.
grounding: Bloomberg Harvard City Leadership Initiative — Data and Evidence case set

seeds.title: Standing up a new department
seeds.summary: Neighborhood engagement function built from nothing inside an existing structure — where it reports, what it is allowed to promise, how it survives a manager change.

seeds.title: Utility shutoff policy
seeds.summary: Delinquency, low-income discount eligibility, and the collection practices the council is comfortable defending publicly.
seeds.note: Abstract away the WA statutory specifics (RCW citations) or set the scenario explicitly in a WA-like state.

seeds.title: Succession cliff
seeds.summary: Three department heads eligible to retire within eighteen months, no internal bench.
grounding: ICMA / Cal-ICMA — Local Governments Preparing the Next Generation (28 case studies)

seeds.title: The verified number
seeds.summary: A council member cites the $18-to-$1 downtown reinvestment ratio in a budget hearing. The manager knows the figure is self-reported and unverified, and also believes the program is probably worth funding.
grounding: Main Street America collective impact statistics

seeds.title: The provider walked away
seeds.summary: A 360-person town's private wastewater provider ceases operations. Continuity of service, capital to acquire or replace, and a CDBG application with a national objective the town must actually meet.
grounding: HUD CDBG project profile — Town of Carlisle

seeds.title: National objective
seeds.summary: A popular streetscape in an inner-ring suburb is proposed for CDBG funding. Staff assumed area benefit without running the LMI numbers, and the tract data is marginal.
grounding: HUD CDBG eligibility and national objective framework

seeds.title: Collaboration without a convener
seeds.summary: Three nonprofits, a hospital, a community college and the city all work the same workforce problem separately. Someone has to convene, and the city has the least money and the most legitimacy.

seeds.title: Ten-year target, two-year manager
seeds.summary: A collaborative committed publicly to a ten-year outcome target. The manager arrives in year three, interim indicators are ambiguous, and the council wants to know whether to keep funding it.

seeds.title: Lead service lines
seeds.summary: A state mandate lands on a city with an aging system, no complete inventory, and disproportionate exposure in lower-income neighborhoods. Sequencing is an engineering, equity and IGR problem at once.
grounding: Chicago Fed community development work on LSL mandates
seeds.note: The strongest community-development / public-works crossover available.

seeds.title: Data capacity
seeds.summary: A rural county wants to target neighborhood investment but has no usable local data, and weaker data quality than an urban peer would have.
grounding: Federal Reserve Board, Putting Data to Work

seeds.title: But for
seeds.summary: A manufacturer requests a ten-year abatement, stating it will locate elsewhere without it. Site selection consultant, no verifiable alternative site, council enthusiastic.

seeds.title: The multiplier in the impact study
seeds.summary: A developer's impact study uses a job multiplier well above what the literature supports. The manager must respond to a study, not a proposal.
grounding: Bartik and Sotherland, Realistic Local Job Multipliers

seeds.title: Race to the bottom
seeds.summary: The adjacent jurisdiction has offered a package to a business currently in your city. Matching costs more than the business is worth; not matching loses it.

seeds.title: Clawback
seeds.summary: Four years into a ten-year agreement the firm has hit its investment commitment but not its job commitment, and it is the largest private employer in town.

seeds.title: Recovery is not restoration
seeds.summary: Eighteen months post-disaster, CDBG-DR funds must be committed. Rebuild the pre-storm base, fund workforce training toward a different one, or market to restore visitors.

seeds.title: Permitting is economic development
seeds.summary: No incentive is on the table. A developer is comparing two jurisdictions on entitlement timeline and carrying cost alone.
seeds.note: The correct answer involves no incentive at all — a good trap for candidates who equate economic development with deals.

seeds.title: Regional or municipal
seeds.summary: Site readiness, a workforce accelerator and a broadband partnership are all available through the regional development organization, but participating means ceding project selection to a regional board.
grounding: NADO Impact Awards — DETCOG SiteSelect, Coastal Bend accelerator, Gage County broadband

seeds.title: Across the boundary
seeds.summary: A city and an adjacent tribal nation both claim regulatory interest in a development straddling the boundary, with a shared utility line and no service agreement.
grounding: HPAIED work on sovereignty and jurisdiction
seeds.note: Deliberately not written yet. The source review asks that tribal material wait for the schema to settle and get a read from someone with tribal government experience before shipping; that review has not happened. Write from the municipal seat — never put the user in the tribal government's chair.

seeds.title: Financing without the usual tool
seeds.summary: An affordable housing deal that cannot access LIHTC. What else assembles the capital stack, and what does the city control?
grounding: New York Fed non-LIHTC case studies (Schenectady, Brooklyn, Jersey City)
seeds.note: Needs a capital stack worked through carefully enough that the numeric part is defensible.
